I found four likely bugs in `lib/core/AxiosError.js`, plus one lower-risk behavior change in `lib/cancel/CanceledError.js`. I read the diff only and did not run the tests.

1. **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:6-12`, `AxiosError.from` drops the original error's properties.** The old version copied every own property of the source error onto the new one, using `toFlatObject`. That included `errno`, `syscall`, `address`, `port`, `response` and the original `stack`. The new version copies only `message`, `code` and `name`.
   - Failure case: a Node `ECONNREFUSED` error converted with `from()` loses `errno`, `syscall` and `address`. Callers that read these properties break.
   - The stack trace now points at the `from()` call site, not where the original error was thrown.

2. **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:7`, `from(null)` or `from(undefined)` now throws.** `error.message` is read without a guard. The old code handled a missing error and fell back to the message `'Error'`. The new code throws a `TypeError` instead of producing an `AxiosError`.

3. **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:9` and `:27`, `cause` and `isAxiosError` are now enumerable own properties.** Before, `cause` was non-enumerable and `isAxiosError` was non-enumerable on the prototype.
   - `cause` is set by plain assignment, so it shows up in `Object.keys`, spreads, `Object.assign` and deep-equality checks. The old code deliberately avoided this ("avoid JSON noise").
   - `isAxiosError` is now an own property, so it is copied by `{...err}` and `toFlatObject`.

4. **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:35`, `status` can now be `undefined`.** The old code set `status` to `null` when the response had no status. The new code assigns `response.status` directly. Code or tests that check `status === null` will break.

5. **`lib/cancel/CanceledError.js:18`, `__CANCEL__` moved from the prototype to an own instance property.** `isCancel` still works. But the property is now enumerable on instances, and it no longer appears on `CanceledError.prototype`. This is minor.

The new tests only check `isNativeError` and the static error codes. None of them cover the `from()` regressions above. I'd add tests for `from()` with extra properties, with a null error, and with a response that has no status.
